title: The summary for Sunday 22 November
text:
Good morning, it is Sunday 22 November: this is the GERICO summary.

Iran. Overnight between Friday and Saturday, Iran attacked Bahrain, home to the US Fifth Fleet. The government in Manama spoke of a fire at a civilian industrial facility, with no injuries. The Revolutionary Guards say they hit American bases, but neither Bahrain nor Washington has confirmed this. Three oil tankers were hit near Hormuz. Tehran has set conditions to reopen the strait, and President Trump has rejected them.

In the Gulf of Finland, the Russian cargo ship Sparta II, linked to Moscow's Defence Ministry, is ablaze following an attack by two drones. The sixteen-person crew was evacuated. Finland considers Ukrainian responsibility likely, though Ukraine has not claimed the action.

Climate. At the COP31 in Antalya, negotiations went past the deadline. The new draft does not mention fossil fuels, but refers back to the COP28 agreement. Approval was expected this morning.

In Mexico, Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, one of the FBI's ten most wanted fugitives, has been captured. At least eleven people died in the clashes, including four soldiers.

In Italy, tomorrow the Budget Committee of the Chamber of Deputies begins examining around seven thousand amendments to the budget law.

Moving on to the markets. Stock markets are closed over the weekend, so the data is from Friday.

Wall Street closed sharply lower. The Nasdaq lost 5.4 per cent, the S&P 500 3.8 per cent, and the Dow Jones 2 per cent. Weighing on the market was Nvidia, which shed around 13 per cent following news of an SEC investigation into its accounting.

In Europe, selling hit stocks linked to artificial intelligence. The FTSE MIB closed down 2.5 per cent, at 48,703 points. The DAX lost 2.6 per cent, the CAC 40 1.9 per cent, and the FTSE 100 1 per cent. In Tokyo, the Nikkei fell by around 5 per cent.

On government bonds, the spread between BTPs and Bunds closed at 109.9 basis points, compared to 103 at the open. The 10-year BTP yield stands at 4.4 per cent.

On commodities, WTI crude closed at $84 a barrel. Gold fell to $3,550 an ounce, after losing more than 9 per cent in a week. TTF gas is up 4.4 per cent, to 88 euros per megawatt-hour, due to lower supplies from Norway and expected cold weather in Europe.

There is no verified exchange rate data in this update.

The full news stories, with sources, are on GERICO. No investment advice.
